notes: The operator first uses \(s(f^{-1}(x))\), but its kernel then uses \(\delta(y-f(x))\); the trace is a sum with denominator \(|1-J_\rho(f)|\).
statement: With \(Ts(x)=\phi(x)s(f(x))\), nondegenerate fixed points give \(\operatorname{tr}^{\,b}T=\sum_{p=f(p)}\operatorname{tr}\phi(p)/|\det_{\mathbb R}(I-df_p)|\). If instead \(Ts(x)=\phi(x)s(f^{-1}(x))\), replace \(f\) by \(f^{-1}\) consistently and assume it is a diffeomorphism.
reconstruction: The denominator bars stand for an absolute determinant in dimensions greater than one. Keeping the initial inverse while retaining the later ordinary-map kernel changes the operator and generally its local weight.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{atiyahbott1964notes}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: The finite-complex trace lemma repeated
notes: The notes again define \(H^i=\ker d/\operatorname{im}d\), require that \(T\) commute with \(d\), and equate the two alternating traces.
statement: For a bounded complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces and a chain endomorphism \(T\), \(\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{tr}T_i=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{tr}H^i(T)\). The Euler-characteristic identity is the specialization \(T=\operatorname{id}\).
reconstruction: The words finite analogue on P000107 supply the intended scope; the formula is not an ordinary-trace identity for the unsmoothed infinite-dimensional section complex.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{atiyahbott1964notes}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: Recovery of the ordinary Lefschetz formula
notes: The first application gives the usual Lefschetz number as the sum of fixed-point multiplicities, written as a sum of signs.
statement: For a smooth self-map of a closed compact real manifold with only nondegenerate fixed points, the de Rham pullback has \(L(f)=\sum_q(-1)^q\operatorname{tr}(f^*|H^q_{\mathrm{dR}}(X))=\sum_{p=f(p)}\operatorname{sgn}\det(I-df_p)\).
reconstruction: The numerator from exterior powers cancels the absolute determinant in the denominator, leaving the local index. At degenerate isolated fixed points the index is still defined, but is not given by this determinant-sign expression.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{atiyahbott1964notes}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: Exterior-power traces give the de Rham numerator
notes: The local trace calculation is abbreviated as \(\operatorname{tr}\varphi_i=\operatorname{det}-1\), followed by eigenvalue products with alternating signs.
statement: For any endomorphism \(A\) of a finite-dimensional vector space, \[\sum_{q=0}^n(-1)^q\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda^q A)=\det(I-A)\]. With \(A=(df_p)^*\), this is the de Rham fibre supertrace.
reconstruction: \ours\ An individual degree trace is not the determinant. The sum over degrees and the determinant argument must be restored; the identity holds without diagonalizability, by polynomial continuity or triangularization.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{atiyahbott1964notes}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: The unresolved complex-case specialization
notes: The complex case mentions holomorphic forms and \(H^{i,0}\), then displays \(|1-J(f)|^2\) in a denominator, \(2\operatorname{Re}(1/(1-J_f))\), and an uncertain conjugate average.
statement: No single equality is determined by these lines. For comparison, the standard holomorphic Lefschetz formula for a holomorphic bundle \(E\) on a compact complex manifold and a nondegenerate holomorphic map with a bundle lift is \(\sum_q(-1)^q\operatorname{tr}(H^q(T):H^q(X,E)\to H^q(X,E))=\sum_p\operatorname{tr}\phi_p/\det_{\mathbb C}(I-df_p)\).
reconstruction: The Dolbeault degree, the bundle being resolved, the meaning of the realification, and the factor in the final average are missing or inconsistent. The displayed comparison formula is not attributed verbatim to the notebook.
fate: The relevant holomorphic specialization is part of \citet{atiyahbott1964notes}, but this does not uniquely repair the source's bidegrees and factors.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the holomorphic fixed-point formula is established; the precise complex-case formula intended on this page is not recoverable with confidence.

title: Real and complex traces and determinants
notes: The last sentence of the complex calculation says that the real trace is the sum of the complex trace and its conjugate; the drawing records \(|a|^2\) for multiplication by \(a\).
statement: For a complex-linear map \(A\), its underlying real map satisfies \(\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbb R}A=2\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbb C}A\) and \(\det_{\mathbb R}A=|\det_{\mathbb C}A|^2\). Thus \(\operatorname{Re}z=(z+\bar z)/2\), whereas the realified trace is the sum, without the factor one-half.
reconstruction: These exact linear-algebra identities clarify the different factors, but do not choose which real or complex Lefschetz number was intended in the preceding unfinished calculation.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{atiyahbott1964notes}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: Projective transformations and eigenlines
notes: Fractional-linear transformations of projective space are named as an application.
statement: If \(A\in GL_{n+1}(\mathbb C)\), fixed points of its projective action on \(\mathbb P^n\) are its invariant lines. For distinct eigenvalues these are \(n+1\) nondegenerate fixed points. The projective transformation acts trivially on \(H^{2q}(\mathbb P^n;\mathbb C)\), so its ordinary Lefschetz number is \(n+1\). Existence of an eigenline holds without the distinct-eigenvalue assumption.
reconstruction: The generic nondegeneracy condition allows direct use of the local formula; repeated eigenvalues require a limiting or ordinary topological fixed-point argument. The notes do not record a formula for a specified transformation.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{atiyahbott1964notes}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: Injective objects and the extension property
notes: An object \(Q\) is called injective when \(\operatorname{Hom}(-,Q)\) is exact; a diagram expresses extension of a morphism from a subobject.
statement: In an abelian category \(\mathcal A\), \(Q\) is injective if every map \(A'\to Q\) extends across every monomorphism \(A'\hookrightarrow A\). Equivalently the contravariant functor \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(-,Q)\) sends each short exact sequence to an exact sequence \(0\to\operatorname{Hom}(A'',Q)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,Q)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A',Q)\to0\).
reconstruction: The variance reverses the order of the sequence. The left exactness of Hom is automatic; surjectivity of the last map is the injectivity condition.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{grothendieck1957homological}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: Enough injectives
notes: The category is said to have enough injectives if every object embeds into an injective; sheaves are given as the example.
statement: An abelian category has enough injectives if for each \(A\) there is a monomorphism \(A\hookrightarrow Q\) with \(Q\) injective. The categories of sheaves of abelian groups, and of modules over a sheaf of unital rings on a space, have enough injectives.
reconstruction: The sheaf example concerns the abelian module category, not the category of coherent sheaves by itself, which usually does not have enough injective objects within that subcategory.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{grothendieck1957homological}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: Right derived functors of a left exact functor
notes: A covariant left exact functor is introduced and its derived functors are required to start with \(F^0=F\).
statement: If \(\mathcal A,\mathcal B\) are abelian categories, \(\mathcal A\) has enough injectives, and \(F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\) is additive and left exact, choose an injective resolution \(A\to I^\bullet\) and define \(R^iF(A)=H^i(F(I^\bullet))\). Comparison maps make the result functorial and independent up to canonical isomorphism of the resolution.
reconstruction: Additivity is made explicit. The superscript denotes right derived functors of a covariant left exact functor, despite the notebook heading's generic use of homology.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{grothendieck1957homological}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the precise statement is a standard established result or definition.

title: The long exact sequence of derived functors
notes: For \(0\to A\to B\to C\to0\), the notes display the beginning of the long exact sequence; the last visible arrow after \(F^1(B)\) is labelled \(\delta\).
statement: Each short exact sequence gives \(0\to F(A)\to F(B)\to F(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^0}R^1F(A)\to R^1F(B)\to R^1F(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^1}R^2F(A)\to\cdots\). Connecting maps go from \(R^iF(C)\) to \(R^{i+1}F(A)\).
reconstruction: The arrow \(R^1F(B)\to R^1F(C)\) is induced by \(B\to C\), not a connecting map. The missing term beyond the frame is not treated as legible source text.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{grothendieck1957homological}.

title: Naturality of the connecting maps
notes: The two short exact sequences are related by a map, and a square is drawn with \(F^0(A)\) at its upper left but \(F^0(C')\) at its lower left; the vertical arrows point upward.
statement: For a morphism of short exact sequences from \(0\to A\to B\to C\to0\) to \(0\to A'\to B'\to C'\to0\), naturality says \(R^{i+1}F(A\to A')\,\delta^i=\delta'^i\,R^iF(C\to C')\). The square has \(R^iF(C)\) and \(R^{i+1}F(A)\) in its top row and the primed counterparts below, with downward induced arrows.
reconstruction: The original square's upper-left letter and the direction of its arrows disagree with the stated morphism of sequences. The modern square is a correction, not a claim that the handwritten A was C.

title: Existence and uniqueness through effaceable delta-functors
notes: The conditions include vanishing \(F^i(Q)=0\) for injectives and a final theorem that the derived functors exist and are unique when there are enough injectives.
statement: The right derived functors form a cohomological \(\delta\)-functor with \(R^0F=F\), natural connecting maps, and \(R^iF(Q)=0\) for injective \(Q\), \(i>0\). Because every object embeds into an injective, the positive-degree functors are effaceable; hence this \(\delta\)-functor is universal and unique up to the unique isomorphism extending the identity of \(F\).
reconstruction: Uniqueness concerns the compatible system of functors and connecting maps. A list of groups with unrelated long exact sequences would not supply the required naturality or universal property.
fate: Already part of the expository framework in \citet{grothendieck1957homological}.

title: Lefschetz number of a geometric endomorphism
notes: For \(\cdots\to\Gamma(E_i)\xrightarrow d\Gamma(E_{i+1})\to\cdots\), the maps \(T_i\) commute with \(d\); the notes define \(L(T,E)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{tr}T_i^*\).
statement: Let \(X\) be a compact smooth manifold without boundary, \((E_\bullet,d)\) a finite elliptic complex, and \(T_i\) continuous endomorphisms of its section spaces satisfying \(d_iT_i=T_{i+1}d_i\). Ellipticity makes \(H^i(E_\bullet)\) finite dimensional. The Lefschetz number is the alternating trace of the induced maps on these cohomology spaces.
reconstruction: Compactness, absence of boundary, finiteness and ellipticity are the analytic setting required by the proof, rather than words repeated at this heading.
fate: Established before this talk. \citep{bott1966report}
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated setting; the notebook occurrence does not leave a separate open problem.

title: Transverse fixed-point formula
notes: The local term is \(\sigma(\rho)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Sp}\varphi_i(\rho)/|\det(1-I_f(\rho))|\); the total is a sum over fixed points.
statement: Assume additionally that \(T_i s(x)=\varphi_i(x)s(f(x))\), where \(f:X\to X\) is smooth and \(\varphi_i:f^*E_i\to E_i\) intertwines the complex. If every fixed point \(\rho\) is transverse, equivalently \(\det(I-df_\rho)\ne0\), then \[L(T,E)=\sum_{f(\rho)=\rho}\frac{\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{tr}\varphi_i(\rho)}{|\det(I-df_\rho)|}.\] There are finitely many such points on compact \(X\).
reconstruction: The geometric form of \(T\), transversality and the fixed-point index of the outer sum are supplied explicitly. The denominator belongs to the real smooth formula; holomorphic variants package numerator and denominator differently.
fate: Bott's Expos\'e 295 states this formula and dates the lecture to November 1965; its bibliography identifies the Atiyah--Bott Harvard notes of fall 1964. Thus later printing does not make the theorem new in this seminar. \citep{bott1966report}
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated setting; the notebook occurrence does not leave a separate open problem.

title: Kernel proof and its trace-class obstruction
notes: The notes call the formal proof trivial: \(L=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{tr}T_i\), with kernel \(\varphi\delta(y-f(x))\); its diagonal gives the fixed-point sum.
statement: The finite-dimensional Euler trace identity does not by itself justify traces on infinite-dimensional section spaces. For a transverse geometric endomorphism the distribution kernel restricts to the diagonal and defines a flat trace; its value is the displayed fixed-point sum. Ordinary operator trace need not exist. A smoothing or complex-power argument is required to identify the alternating flat trace with the cohomological trace.

title: Complex-power regularization and eigenspace cancellation

title: Off-diagonal regularity and the value at zero

title: Multiplying distributions conormal to transverse submanifolds

title: Finite type and coherent algebraic sheaves

title: A value-distribution route to spectral completeness

title: Left--right equivalence and structural stability of map germs

title: The perturbation of a complex square by a conjugate-linear term

title: Iterated coranks and the fold--cusp Boardman symbols
notes: A decreasing rank sequence is introduced on P000114; P000115 changes to a corank convention, calls \(\Sigma_0\) regular, and labels a cusp \(\Sigma_{10}\).
statement: With Boardman's convention, the first entry is \(\dim\ker df\), and successive entries are obtained by intrinsic derivative or Jacobian-ideal extensions. title: Boardman strata in jet space and generic transversality

title: Smooth, analytic and formal equivalence are different categories

title: Infinitesimal stability and the source--target linearization

Properness, the topology of maps, and the global or multigerm setting matter; an arbitrary Frechet-space inverse-function theorem does not prove the assertion.

title: Natural metric tensors from curvature and its derivatives

statement: A finite-order natural tensor constructed from a Riemannian metric is determined in normal coordinates by the curvature tensor and finitely many covariant derivatives, equivariantly under changes of orthonormal frame. For polynomial natural tensors, invariant theory expresses them using tensor products, permutations and contractions with the metric and its inverse (and the volume tensor in an oriented setting). A general smooth natural invariant need only be a smooth function of such data; it need not be polynomial.

title: Normal-coordinate metric coefficients and their identities
notes: The source expands the metric without a linear term and says that all coefficients in a normal system are tensors; the Taylor terms carry the indices \(\gamma\delta\) and \(\gamma\delta\varepsilon\).

title: Analytic and formal Weierstrass division
notes: The stated division is \(f=PQ+\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}b_i(u)y^i\), with coefficients and quotient of the same class; the quotient by \((P)\) is finite over the parameter ring.

The analogous formal statement holds over characteristic-zero formal power-series rings. The analytic or formal quotient by \((P)\) is free of rank \(n\) over the parameter germ ring, with basis \(1,y,\ldots,y^{n-1}\). This is finite module rank, not finite dimension over the scalar field when parameters remain.

title: The flat-function counterexample to unique division

title: Type decomposition on a holomorphic bundle
notes: \(d=d'+d''\), \(D=D'+D''\), with bidegrees \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\); the notes call these two connections.

title: Existence and uniqueness of the Chern connection

title: Whitney example with five branches
notes: The example is \(xy(y-x)(y-xz)(x\varphi(z)-y)\), with \(\varphi(0)=0\) and \(\varphi\) transcendental; the notes say four surfaces but later use the two quadruples \((1,2,3,4)\) and \((1,2,3,5)\).

The five factors define five smooth surface germs meeting along the \(z\)-axis, with generically distinct tangent planes away from exceptional axis points. This is the Whitney-type construction of an analytic three-variable germ whose zero-set geometry obstructs polynomialization by a smooth local diffeomorphism. Its critical locus is nonisolated, so it does not contradict finite determinacy at isolated critical points.

title: The pair of cross-ratios obstructs algebraic realization
notes: The anharmonic ratio of tangent planes through a common line is called a diffeomorphism invariant. A curve in the two cross-ratio coordinates is transcendental for the example but would be algebraic for a polynomial.
statement: Modulo the common tangent line, five tangent planes give five points of a projective line. A local diffeomorphism acts by one projective linear transformation on this normal plane, hence preserves the two cross-ratios formed using the first three marked planes. After fixed rational changes of cross-ratio coordinates, the resulting parameterized curve is \(z\mapsto(z,\varphi(z))\). A polynomial configuration yields an algebraic cross-ratio relation along its algebraic multiple-branch locus; choosing \(\varphi\) algebraically transcendental contradicts that relation. Permuting the finitely many branches only applies finitely many rational coordinate changes and does not remove the obstruction.

A smooth steady unforced Euler solution satisfies \((v\cdot

title: Arnold analytic decomposition of a stationary flow
notes: For an analytic stationary velocity in a bounded domain, not everywhere collinear with its curl, finitely many analytic pieces separate cells with torus windings or cylindrical rotations.
statement: Let \(D\) be a connected compact three-dimensional real-analytic Riemannian domain with real-analytic boundary, and let \(v\) be a real-analytic stationary incompressible Euler field tangent to the boundary, analytic up to it. Assume \(v\times\operatorname{curl}v\) is not identically zero. Outside a proper compact analytic exceptional set, regular Bernoulli level components are embedded tori or annuli. On a torus the streamlines are conjugate to a constant linear flow and hence are closed or dense; on an annulus they are closed. The critical values of the Bernoulli function, including its boundary restriction, determine finitely many regular cells.

title: A common first integral for two commuting divergence-free fields
notes: The compact-orbit proof writes \(\operatorname{rot}(a\ast b)=0\), then calls \(a\times b\) a differential and identifies orbits with level surfaces.
statement: On an oriented volume three-manifold \((M,\mu)\), if \(a,b\) preserve \(\mu\) and commute, the one-form \(\alpha=\iota_b\iota_a\mu\) is closed. If \(H^1(M;\mathbb R)=0\), then \(\alpha=dF\). Both fields are tangent to the levels of \(F\). Where they are independent, \(dF\ne0\), and their joint orbit is open in the connected regular level component. This last step does not identify a singular-level orbit with an entire closed level set.

title: A compact regular joint orbit is a torus
notes: The notes say that compact orbits without boundary are tori, with the one-parameter velocity action giving a winding.
statement: Let \(C\) be a compact connected regular level surface without boundary on which the two commuting fields \(a,b\) are everywhere independent and tangent. Their complete flows define a locally free \(\mathbb R^2\)-action. Every orbit is open; connectedness makes the action transitive, so \(C\simeq\mathbb R^2/\Lambda\) for a discrete cocompact subgroup \(\Lambda\), necessarily a rank-two lattice. Thus \(C\simeq T^2\), and either field is a constant linear flow in these action coordinates. Its individual streamline may be dense and nonclosed although the joint \(\mathbb R^2\)-orbit is compact.
reconstruction: \ours{} The action-and-lattice argument supplies the rank and completeness qualifications. Compact joint orbits are not confused with compact or closed individual streamlines.

title: The assertion that every joint orbit is compact is false
notes: The separately labelled mathematical theorem assumes \(b_1=0\), a compact manifold, and two commuting divergence-free fields, and concludes that their orbits are compact.
statement: These hypotheses do not force compact joint orbits. On the round \(S^3\subset\mathbb C^2\), let \(a(z_1,z_2)=(iz_1,i\alpha z_2)\), with \(\alpha\notin\mathbb Q\), and let \(b=0\). Both fields are smooth, complete and divergence-free, they commute, and \(H^1(S^3;\mathbb R)=0\). Through a point with \(z_1z_2\ne0\), the joint \(\mathbb R^2\)-orbit equals the irrational \(a\)-orbit and is dense but nonclosed in a Clifford torus, hence noncompact. The common first integral here is constant; its level set is not the orbit.

fate: Arnold's published proof only uses compact regular Bernoulli components with two independent tangent fields, as in item 1965-76.6; it does not state this unrestricted compact-orbit lemma. \citep{arnold1966geometrie}

title: Boundary components give annuli with closed streamlines
notes: The notes say that noncompact orbits are cylinders and illustrate fluid between rotating coaxial cylinders, with neighboring rings turning in opposite directions.
statement: For a compact regular Bernoulli level component \(C\) meeting the boundary transversely in Arnold's setting, each boundary component is a closed velocity orbit. Commutation and independence propagate its period through \(C\), and \(C\) is an annulus with closed streamlines. It is not a theorem that every noncompact two-dimensional orbit of an \(\mathbb R^2\)-action is a cylinder: a trivial stabilizer gives a plane, while a rank-one stabilizer gives a cylinder. The rotating-cylinder sketch is a qualitative illustration and does not by itself establish an inviscid or viscous Taylor--Couette instability theorem.

Smooth initial data yield the corresponding classical solution. title: Hamiltonian spectral symmetry in the inviscid limit
notes: At \(\nu=0\) the spectrum is said to be symmetric about both axes, with a partly unclear Hamiltonian parenthesis.
statement: For a real finite-dimensional Hamiltonian linearization \(A=JH\), where \(J\) is invertible skew-symmetric and \(H\) symmetric, eigenvalues occur with their algebraic multiplicities in the set \(\lambda,-\lambda,\overline\lambda,-\overline\lambda\). Reality gives conjugation and the Hamiltonian identity gives sign symmetry. For Euler's infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian/Poisson operator, an analogous assertion requires a specified symplectic leaf, operator domains and a distinction between point and continuous spectrum; the finite-dimensional matrix statement alone is not a complete theorem about the PDE spectrum.

title: The unreadable conditional spectral-stability theorem
notes: A conditional theorem says that if an inviscid stable flow exists, its spectrum looks like the adjacent unlabelled sketch. A nearby Poiseuille remark calls a flow exceptional without specifying geometry or parameters.
statement: The sketch does not determine a precise spectral theorem. In a finite-dimensional Hamiltonian linearization, Lyapunov stability rules out eigenvalues with positive real part, and sign symmetry then puts eigenvalues on the imaginary axis; this does not by itself imply semisimplicity of a zero eigenvalue or nonlinear stability from spectral information. A Poiseuille-flow assertion would require planar or pipe geometry, boundary conditions, Reynolds number, perturbation space and the intended notion of instability.

title: Inertia operator and the left-invariant Riemannian metric
notes: \(L:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak g^*\) is symmetric positive definite and \(\langle a,b\rangle_g=\langle dL_{g^{-1}}a,dL_{g^{-1}}b\rangle_e\).
statement: On a finite-dimensional Lie group \(G\), a symmetric positive-definite linear isomorphism \(\mathcal I:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak g^*\) defines \(\langle u,v\rangle_e=(\mathcal Iu)(v)\). Left translation gives a Riemannian metric, with inertia map \(\mathcal I_g=(dL_{g^{-1}})^*\mathcal I\,dL_{g^{-1}}:T_gG\to T_g^*G\). In infinite dimensions a weak positive metric need not identify the tangent space with its full continuous dual; that extra functional-analytic conclusion is not automatic.
reconstruction: The symbol \(\mathcal I\) distinguishes inertia from left translation. The exact tangent/cotangent placement repairs the ambiguity in the lower arrows of the handwritten diagram.
fate: Established before this talk. \citep{arnold1966geometrie}
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated setting; the notebook occurrence does not leave a separate open problem.

title: Free rigid-body motion as a geodesic on SO(3)
notes: For \(G=SO(3)\), geodesics describe rotation of a rigid body about a fixed point; the metric is kinetic energy.
statement: For a rigid body with a fixed point and no applied torque, the positive inertia tensor defines a left-invariant kinetic-energy metric on \(SO(3)\). Its geodesics are precisely the free rotations, with the usual factor \(1/2\) in kinetic energy. An asymmetric top generally has a left-invariant metric that is not bi-invariant; no external potential or torque is included.
fate: Arnold presents this as the classical Euler rigid-body model motivating the general group construction. \citep{arnold1966geometrie}
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated setting; the notebook occurrence does not leave a separate open problem.

title: Euler flow as a geodesic of the right-invariant L2 metric
notes: \(G=\operatorname{SDiff}D\), \(\langle a,b\rangle=\int_D(a,b)\,dx\), and ideal-fluid flows are geodesics; this follows the preceding left-invariant construction without a stated change of convention.
statement: For an oriented compact Riemannian domain, smooth fluid motions that preserve volume \(\eta_t\) with impermeable boundary are critical points of kinetic action for the right-invariant \(L^2\) metric on volume-preserving diffeomorphisms. The Eulerian velocity \(v=\dot\eta_t\circ\eta_t^{-1}\) satisfies the incompressible Euler equation. Inversion converts right-invariant to left-invariant notation and changes the associated velocity/bracket convention. A rigorous infinite-dimensional geodesic-flow existence theorem needs an appropriate Sobolev manifold and regularity analysis; the smooth formal identification alone does not supply it.
reconstruction: The physical particle map uses right invariance. The explicit convention change prevents importing the left-invariant sign into Eulerian velocity formulas. The functional-analytic existence question is separated from this variational identity.
fate: Arnold's 1966 paper, section 10, pp. 344--345, gives the exact right-invariant fluid interpretation and explains the sign change from the earlier left-invariant convention. This is the full post-talk source checked here; its introduction also mentions 1965 announcements, without a priority claim being made for this occurrence. \citep{arnold1966geometrie}
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this is an established result in the stated setting; the notebook occurrence does not leave a separate open problem.

title: The affine group realizes the hyperbolic plane
notes: For \(G=\{x\mapsto ax+b:a>0\}\), the notes identify the resulting dynamics with the geodesic flow on the Lobachevsky plane and ask to inspect the invariant metric.
statement: Write group coordinates as \((b,a)\) with \(a>0\) and multiplication \((b,a)(b',a')=(b+ab',aa')\). Declaring the dilation and translation generators orthonormal at the identity gives the left-invariant metric \(ds^2=(db^2+da^2)/a^2\). This is the standard upper-half-plane hyperbolic metric of curvature \(-1\), so its geodesic flow realizes the stated example. Different overall metric scales change the curvature normalization.

title: The bilinear metric-adjoint operation B
notes: \(\langle[a,b],c\rangle=\langle b,B(c,a)\rangle\).
statement: On a finite-dimensional metric Lie algebra, this identity uniquely defines \(B(c,a)=\operatorname{ad}_a^{\dagger}c\), the metric adjoint of \(b\mapsto[a,b]\). It is bilinear and satisfies \(\langle B(c,a),b\rangle+\langle B(c,b),a\rangle=0\). For a weak infinite-dimensional metric, existence of such an adjoint in the chosen smooth Lie algebra must be established separately. This record defines \(B\); its evolution equation appears in the following record.

title: Left and right trivializations of tangent and cotangent vectors
notes: The lower diagram places \(T_gG\) between two copies of the Lie algebra, with downward inertia maps and dual arrows in the bottom row; the last star and one lower arrow are overwritten.
statement: For a tangent velocity \(\dot g\), the left and right trivializations are \(u=dL_{g^{-1}}\dot g\) and \(w=dR_{g^{-1}}\dot g\). Their dual maps send Lie-algebra covectors to covectors at \(g\), with arrows contravariant to tangent maps. The left-invariant inertia square commutes by \(\mathcal I_g=(dL_{g^{-1}})^*\mathcal I\,dL_{g^{-1}}\). The same fixed \(\mathcal I\) in a right-hand square would require a right-invariant metric, unless an appropriate transformed inertia is inserted. The overwritten terminal node is read mathematically as a dual algebra, not as evidence for a bidual identification.

title: Weyl algebras with central parameters and their fraction fields
notes: \(R_{n,k}\) is the ring of differential operators in \(n\) variables with \(k\) commuting parameters; \(D_{n,k}\) is its division ring of ratios.

Then \(\operatorname{gr}R_{n,k}\) is the corresponding commutative polynomial domain. For nonzero \(a,b\), degree is additive and \(\sigma(ab)=\sigma(a)\sigma(b)\). The principal-symbol map is multiplicative on nonzero elements, not an additive map from the filtered ring to its graded ring.

notes: For \(b=a_1a_2^{-1}\), the notes take \([a_1]/[a_2]\) and say that it depends only on \(b\), not its representation. The short continuation at the right edge is uncertain.

It is not a division-ring homomorphism.

title: A universal determinant over a division ring
notes: \ru{Универс. det --- отобр. в фактор по коммутанту. То же в теле, универс. --- ?}
statement: For a division ring \(D\), what is the abelianization of the stable general linear group? The answer is \[K_1(D)=\mathrm{GL}_{\infty}(D)_{\mathrm{ab}}\simeq D^{\times}/[D^{\times},D^{\times}].\] The Dieudonn\'e determinant realizes this quotient; every group homomorphism from the stable general linear group to an abelian group factors uniquely through it. In characteristic zero this also holds in each finite matrix size at least two.

title: Determine all automorphisms of the Weyl division ring
notes: \ru{Найти все автоморфизмы этого тела (тр. зад.)}; below it: \ru{(Пр. Фурье + умн. на ф-ю)}.
statement: For the previously defined \(D_{n,k}\), determine its automorphisms over the coefficient field. A precise minimal case is \(\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb C}D_{1,0}\), where \(D_{1,0}=Q(\mathbb C\langle x,p\mid px-xp=1\rangle)\). The question concerns the division ring, not just automorphisms or endomorphisms of its polynomial Weyl subalgebra.

fate: Polynomial automorphisms are understood \citep{makarlimanov1984automorphisms}; rational subfield stabilizers are classified by \citet[Proposition 2.2]{alevdumas1998invariants}. These are partial answers to the notebook\textquotesingle s unrestricted question.

title: Fourier transforms and multiplication as automorphism constructions
notes: The parenthesis to the automorphism problem suggests Fourier transform plus multiplication by a function.
statement: For \(D_{1,0}\) with \([p,x]=1\), the algebraic Fourier map \(x\mapsto p\), \(p\mapsto-x\) is an automorphism. For \(u\in\mathbb C(x)^{\times}\), conjugation by multiplication by \(u\) gives \(x\mapsto x\), \(p\mapsto p-u^{\prime}/u\). Multiplication alone is not a unital algebra automorphism. More generally every rational shift \(p\mapsto p+h(x)\) is an automorphism, but need not be inner.

title: Growth dimension and the missing logarithm
notes: For generators \(\alpha=(a_1,\ldots,a_s)\), the displayed numerator is \(d(\alpha,N)\), described as the number of linearly independent monomials of degree at most \(N\); the denominator is \(\ln N\).
statement: The correct algebra growth invariant is \[\operatorname{GKdim}_L A=\sup_V\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log\dim_L V^N}{\log N},\] where \(V\) runs over finite-dimensional \(L\)-subspaces containing \(1\), and \(V^N\) is the span of products of at most \(N\) factors. title: Fourier-side kernel and stabilization at infinity
notes: The notes set \(\sigma=\sigma_\infty+\sigma^{\prime}\), call \(\sigma^{\prime}\) finite in \(\xi\), and give a Fourier-side integral with \(\widehat{\sigma^{\prime}}(\xi-\eta,\eta)\).
statement: For a symbol equal to \(\sigma_\infty(\xi)\) outside a compact set in \(x\), \(\widehat{Au}(\xi)=\sigma_\infty(\xi)\widehat u(\xi)+(2\pi)^{-n}\int\widehat{\sigma^{\prime}}_x(\xi-\eta,\eta)\widehat u(\eta)\,d\eta\), with the corresponding normalization adjustment for a unitary transform.
reconstruction: Compact support must refer to \(x\) in this argument. A nonzero homogeneous function cannot be compactly supported in \(\xi\). The scan itself says \(\xi\); this is a notebook slip, not a transcription error.
fate: This representation is part of the 1965 calculus; compare \citet{agranovich1965elliptic} and the independently published \citet{kohnnirenberg1965algebra}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; no unresolved problem is asserted by this occurrence.

title: Smooth equivalence and rough-symbol inequivalence
notes: The two definitions are said to agree for smooth symbols but to lead to different classes after smoothness is relaxed.
statement: Left/right quantizations have the same principal symbol in a smooth classical calculus. For rough symbols, boundedness and the ability to convert quantizations require explicit regularity; no equivalence follows merely from the formal integral expressions.
reconstruction: The notes do not specify a pair of rough symbol spaces for a sharp inequivalence theorem. This occurrence records the methodological warning, not an unrecorded counterexample.
fate: Already treated in \citet{agranovich1965elliptic}, especially \S\S6--8; this is expository by the date of the talk.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; no unresolved problem is asserted by this occurrence.

title: Sobolev scale and order convention
notes: \(\|u\|_\ell^2=\int(1+|\xi|^2)^\ell|\widehat u|^2\); an order-\(s\) operator maps \(H^\ell\) to \(H^{\ell-s}\).
statement: For symbols in the smooth uniform class \(S^s_{1,0}\), or for properly supported local operators, \(A:H^\ell_{\mathrm{comp}}\to H^{\ell-s}_{\mathrm{loc}}\) continuously. Uniform global symbol estimates give the global bounded map on \(\mathbb R^n\).

title: Angular Sobolev regularity sufficient for L2 boundedness
notes: The displayed criterion assumes \(q>(n-1)/2\) and \(\sup_x\|\sigma(x,\cdot)\|_{H^q(S^{n-1})}<\infty\).
statement: For \(n\geq2\), a degree-zero symbol measurable in \(x\) with \[M=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_x\sum_{m,k}(1+m)^{2q}|a_{mk}(x)|^2<\infty\], \(q>(n-1)/2\), defines an \(L^2\)-bounded left-quantized operator. Its norm is at most a dimensional constant times \(M^{1/2}\).
reconstruction: The weight \(1+m\) retains the constant harmonic; the printed use of \(m\) alone is harmless only after separating multiplication.
fate: \citet{agranovich1965elliptic}, Proposition 7.1 and Remark 7.1, already give the criterion and its rough-base-variable interpretation.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; no unresolved problem is asserted by this occurrence.

title: Addition theorem and the boundedness proof
notes: The proof uses Schwarz, the sum \(\sum_k|Y_{mk}|^2\), and a series with exponent \(n-2\). Several factors and signs in the handwritten estimates are lost or reversed.
statement: Pointwise Schwarz gives \(|Au(x)|^2\leq M\sum_{m,k}(1+m)^{-2q}|Y_{mk}(D)u(x)|^2\). Plancherel and the addition theorem give \(\|Au\|_2^2\leq C M\|u\|_2^2\sum_m(1+m)^{n-2-2q}\). The last series converges exactly when \(2q>n-1\).
reconstruction: \ours{} The explanatory verification here is supplied by us for the established result or correction. The two Schwarz sums are multiplied, not equated; \(|\widehat u|^2\) remains under the Fourier integral, and the weight in the second sum has exponent \(-2q\). These are mathematical repairs to handwriting verified in the scans.
fate: The complete estimate is in \citet{agranovich1965elliptic}, proof of Proposition 7.1.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; no unresolved problem is asserted by this occurrence.

title: Endpoint and absence of base-variable smoothness
notes: The notes say \ru{По $\xi$ гладк. не нужно} near the angular argument and discuss divergence at the limiting exponent.
statement: The angular criterion needs no regularity in \(x\). At \(q=(n-1)/2\), its proof gives a harmonic series and no uniform bound; individual operators, such as the identity, remain bounded. The endpoint is not a claim that every symbol there is unbounded.
reconstruction: In this local context the handwritten \(\xi\) must be \(x\); otherwise it contradicts the angular hypothesis. A later, different criterion genuinely removes angular regularity.
fate: \citet{agranovich1965elliptic}, Remark 7.1, discusses the sharp failure of the general convergence assertion.

title: Kernel version of the angular criterion
notes: For \(K(x,z)=k(x,z/|z|)|z|^{-n}\), the threshold becomes \(q>-1/2\).
statement: If \(k(x,\cdot)\) has zero spherical mean, is measurable in \(x\), and is uniformly in \(H^q(S^{n-1})\), \(q>-1/2\), then the associated distributional singular integral is \(L^2\)-bounded. For negative \(q\), the angular kernel is interpreted as a distribution.
reconstruction: The harmonic transform raises the angular Sobolev index by \(n/2\). Cancellation and the distributional interpretation are essential.
fate: \citet{agranovich1965elliptic}, \S\S6--7, contains the symbol-to-kernel transfer.

title: Planar Riesz-transform example
statement: In \(\mathbb R^2\), \(\operatorname{pv}z_1/|z|^3\) is, up to the Fourier normalization and sign, the kernel of the first Riesz transform, whose multiplier is a constant times \(i\xi_1/|\xi|\); it is \(L^2\)-bounded.

title: A complementary criterion using base-variable derivatives
notes: Compactly supported dependence on \(x\) with \(n+1\) derivatives gives Fourier decay \((1+|\xi-\eta|^2)^{-(n+1)/2}\).
statement: If \(\sigma^{\prime}(\cdot,\eta)\) is supported in one fixed compact set and its \(x\)-derivatives through order \(n+1\) are uniformly bounded, then \(|\widehat{\sigma^{\prime}}_x(\zeta,\eta)|\leq C(1+|\zeta|)^{-n-1}\). The Fourier kernel is dominated by an \(L^1\) convolution kernel, hence defines a bounded \(L^2\) operator, without angular smoothness.
reconstruction: Uniformity in \(\eta\) and fixed spatial support are supplied; boundedness of the separate multiplier \(\sigma_\infty\) is also needed.
fate: Already treated in \citet{agranovich1965elliptic}, especially \S\S6--8; this is expository by the date of the talk.

title: First symbolic composition rule
notes: The notes announce that \(AB-\sigma_1\sigma_2(x,D)\) is subordinate.
statement: For smooth classical operators of orders \(s_1,s_2\), \(AB-\operatorname{Op}(\sigma_{s_1}(A)\sigma_{s_2}(B))\) has order at most \(s_1+s_2-1\), provided the representative operators have only the stated principal homogeneous term plus lower-order remainders.
reconstruction: Proper support is understood locally. Rough-symbol boundedness alone does not imply this calculus.
fate: The result precedes the seminar in \citet{agranovich1965elliptic} and \citet{kohnnirenberg1965algebra}; record 84 continues its proof.

title: Pseudolocality and localization
notes: Pseudolocality and extension to manifolds are announced.
statement: For a smooth pseudodifferential operator, \(\operatorname{sing\,supp}(Au)\subseteq\operatorname{sing\,supp}(u)\). If smooth compact cutoffs have disjoint supports, \(\varphi A\psi\) has a smooth kernel.

title: Left and right quantizations differ below principal order
notes: The Fourier kernel uses either \(\sigma(\xi-\eta,\eta)\) or \(\sigma(\xi-\eta,\xi)\); Taylor expansion makes their difference subordinate.
statement: For a smooth symbol of order \(s\), left and right quantizations using the same symbol agree modulo order \(s-1\). The full conversion is an asymptotic series involving mixed base and frequency derivatives.

title: Adjoint principal symbol
notes: The adjoint reverses the two quantizations and conjugates the symbol.
statement: With a fixed smooth positive density and Hermitian metrics, the formal adjoint of an order-\(s\) operator has principal symbol \(\sigma_s(A)^*\), the fiberwise Hermitian transpose. The remainder is of order \(s-1\).
reconstruction: For scalar operators the star is complex conjugation. Density and bundle metrics matter only below the leading symbol in a compatible local trivialization.

notes: Gelfand asks \ru{Можно ли зам. многочл. на другие, чтобы получ. та же алгебра.}

title: Cotangent location of the principal symbol
notes: The lecture ends by placing the symbol on the cotangent bundle.
statement: The scalar principal symbol of an order-\(s\) operator is a degree-\(s\) homogeneous function on \(T^*M\setminus0\); for operators between bundles it is a section of \(\operatorname{Hom}(\pi^*E,\pi^*F)\).
reconstruction: The bundle-valued statement is the modern completion of the scalar shorthand; record 84 supplies the coordinate argument.

title: Reconstruction from k-plane integrals and economical families
notes: Reconstruct \(f\) from \(\varphi(h)=\int_hf\); for lines in \(\mathbb R^3\), can the four-parameter data be reduced to three parameters?
statement: For a rapidly decreasing smooth function on affine space, recover \(f\) from its integrals over affine \(k\)-planes. For a prescribed smaller family, an inversion question additionally requires its geometry and a nonvanishing inversion coefficient; mere equality of parameter counts does not imply injectivity.
reconstruction: The first question is precise. The three-parameter subfamily is not specified; later cycle formulas answer an appropriate family-dependent version, not every subfamily.
fate: Published soon after in \citet{gelfand1967planes}; the relevant definitions and Theorems 1--2 were checked in the Russian full text.
present_status: As of November 2026: the full-data problem and admissible cycle inversions are established; the unspecified economical-family sentence does not define a further open problem.

title: Affine-plane bundle and translation-incidence section
notes: \(H_{n,k}\) consists of affine \(k\)-planes with volume data, \(G\) records parallel classes, and \(S_\beta\) selects the translate through \(\beta\).
statement: An affine plane is \(\alpha+b\), where \(\alpha\in\operatorname{Gr}(k,\mathbb F^n)\) and \(b\in\mathbb F^n/\alpha\), with compatible real or complex volume normalization. The pullback \(\varphi(\alpha,\beta)\) depends only on \(\beta\bmod\alpha\).
reconstruction: Volume weights must transform with a change of frame. The real and complex versions use different integration densities; they cannot be interchanged without a normalization convention.
fate: Published soon after in \citet{gelfand1967planes}; the relevant definitions and Theorems 1--2 were checked in the Russian full text.

title: Determinant of vector entries paired with a symmetric form
notes: For a symmetric \(k\)-linear form \(B\), the notes define a signed sum over permutations of entries \(\xi_{ij}\).
statement: For vectors \(\xi_{ij}\in W\), set \(\det_B(\xi)=\sum_{\pi\in S_k}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)B(\xi_{1\pi(1)},\ldots,\xi_{k\pi(k)})\). Symmetry of \(B\) makes this alternating in rows and columns. If \(B\) vanishes whenever an argument belongs to \(\alpha\), the expression descends to \(W/\alpha\).
reconstruction: This is a polarized determinant, not a determinant with an unspecified multiplication on \(W\).

title: Translation derivatives define a differential form on directions
notes: The symmetric derivative \(\partial_\beta^k\varphi\) and nearby frames \(e_i+\xi_{ij}\) produce a \(k\)-form; frame-independence is Theorem 1.
statement: The identification \(T_\alpha\operatorname{Gr}(k,\mathbb F^n)=\operatorname{Hom}(\alpha,\mathbb F^n/\alpha)\) lets the polarized determinant pair the translation derivative with \(k\) tangent directions. The accompanying frame-volume factor makes the result intrinsic. In the complex formulation the corresponding object has bidegree \((k,k)\), with holomorphic and antiholomorphic derivative factors.
reconstruction: The real \(k\)-form and complex \((k,k)\)-form are distinguished explicitly. Indexing a basis of \(\alpha\) uses \(k\) entries, even where the notebook writes \(n\).
fate: Published soon after in \citet{gelfand1967planes}; the relevant definitions and Theorems 1--2 were checked in the Russian full text.

title: Closedness characterizes the range with restricted k and decay
notes: Theorem 2 says \(\varphi\) is in the plane-transform range if and only if its associated form is closed.
statement: In the smooth rapidly decreasing class \(\Phi\) of the published theorem, with rapid decay in the translation variable together with all derivatives, and \(1\leq k<n-1\), the Gelfand--Graev--Shapiro closedness equations characterize the transform range. The paper gives the complex theorem and notes its real analogue. The case \(k=n-1\) is excluded.
reconstruction: These hypotheses are restored from the published Theorem 1, not inferred from the short notebook theorem. For hyperplanes, closedness in top degree cannot substitute for the missing global moment conditions.
fate: \citet{gelfand1967planes}, Theorem 1, p. 23 of the Russian edition, and its two footnotes explicitly impose the restriction and discuss the real version.
present_status: As of November 2026: established for the published range class; the unrestricted notebook wording is not a valid universal characterization.

title: Cycle inversion and its homological coefficient
notes: Theorem 3 states \(\int_\gamma\kappa\varphi=C_\gamma f(\beta)\); \(C_\gamma\) is topological.
statement: For transform data \(\varphi=R_k f\) and an admissible closed cycle in the direction Grassmannian, integration of the associated form through \(\beta\) equals a fixed homological pairing times \(f(\beta)\). The cycle has real dimension \(k\) in the real construction and \(2k\) in the complex construction. It yields inversion only if its pairing is nonzero.
reconstruction: Orientations, density normalization and the relevant homology class determine \(C_\gamma\). A merely parameter-counting choice of cycle is insufficient.
fate: \citet{gelfand1967planes}, Theorem 2 and the subsequent cycle calculation, pp. 29--31, establish this formula.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; no unresolved problem is asserted by this occurrence.

title: Nonzero complex coefficient is an existence statement
notes: The notes suggest that in the complex case the coefficient is always nonzero, with a contrast to real parity.
statement: For complex affine \(k\)-planes there exist \(2k\)-cycles with nonzero inversion coefficient. An arbitrary cycle can have zero coefficient, including a null-homologous cycle or the zero class. The real local differential inversion has the familiar parity obstruction for odd \(k\).
reconstruction: \ours{} The explanatory verification here is supplied by us for the established result or correction. The published theorem has an existential quantifier. This is a substantive correction to the literal universal wording, not a new open case.
fate: \citet{gelfand1967planes}, Theorem 2, states existence of a suitable nonzero class; it does not assert nonvanishing on every cycle.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; no unresolved problem is asserted by this occurrence.

title: Delta-current form of the inversion identity
notes: The notes give the distributional identity \(C_\gamma\delta_\beta=\int_\gamma\kappa\delta_h\).
statement: Interpret plane integration as pairing with the plane delta distribution. Applying the derivative-form construction and then integrating over the admissible cycle gives the evaluation current \(C_\gamma\delta_\beta\), with the same conventions as the function inversion theorem.
reconstruction: The formula is an equality of distributions, after pairing with test functions; it is not a pointwise product of delta functions.
fate: Published soon after in \citet{gelfand1967planes}; the relevant definitions and Theorems 1--2 were checked in the Russian full text.

title: Complex-line coordinates and the (1,1)-form
notes: Lines are written \(x=\alpha t+\beta\), with integration \(dt\,d\bar t\); a form involving \(\partial_{\beta_i}d\alpha_i\) and its conjugate is displayed.
statement: On the graph chart \(x_j=\alpha_jx_n+\beta_j\), \(j=1,\ldots,n-1\), the line space has complex dimension \(2(n-1)\). Up to the volume factor, the form is \(\kappa\varphi=\sum_{i,j}\partial_{\beta_i}\partial_{\bar\beta_j}\varphi\,d\alpha_i\wedge d\bar\alpha_j\).
reconstruction: Writing arbitrary \(n\)-vectors \(\alpha,\beta\) introduces the reparametrizations \((\alpha,\beta)\sim(\lambda\alpha,\beta+t_0\alpha)\). The graph chart removes this redundancy and fixes the derivative order.
fate: Published soon after in \citet{gelfand1967planes}; the relevant definitions and Theorems 1--2 were checked in the Russian full text.

title: Euler angles and a curve in SO(3)
notes: A motion of the top is a curve in \(SO(3)\), factored as successive rotations with angles \(\varphi,\theta,\psi\).
statement: A fixed-point rigid-body attitude is \(R(t)\in SO(3)\). Away from the polar coordinate singularities it admits Euler-angle coordinates, with the middle angle \(\theta\) measuring the inclination of the body axis.

notes: \(T=\tfrac12(\dot\varphi^2+\dot\psi^2+2\dot\varphi\dot\psi\cos\theta+\dot\theta^2)\), \(V=p\cos\theta\).
statement: For equal normalized principal moments of inertia and potential \(V=p\cos\theta\), set \(L=T-V\). The coordinates \(\varphi,\psi\) are cyclic and energy \(h=T+p\cos\theta\) is conserved.

title: Correct cyclic momenta
notes: The handwritten first integrals contain \(\dot\varphi+2\dot\psi\cos\theta=n\) and \(\dot\psi+2\dot\varphi\cos\theta=e\).
statement: Differentiation of the recorded \(L\) gives \(n=\dot\varphi+\dot\psi\cos\theta\), \(e=\dot\psi+\dot\varphi\cos\theta\). Thus for \(u=\cos\theta\), \(\dot\varphi=(n-eu)/(1-u^2)\), \(\dot\psi=(e-nu)/(1-u^2)\), when \(|u|<1\).

title: The cubic governing nutation
notes: Elimination leads to \(dt=du/\sqrt{U(u)}\), where \(U\) is indicated as cubic but not completely expanded.
statement: With the corrected momenta, \(\dot u^2=U(u)=2(h-pu)(1-u^2)-n^2-e^2+2neu\). Equivalently, \(U(u)=2pu^3-2hu^2+2(ne-p)u+2h-n^2-e^2\). Physical intervals also require \(|u|\leq1\) and \(U(u)\geq0\).

title: Elliptic quadrature and degenerate limits
notes: The top of P000133 identifies the integral as elliptic.
statement: For a cubic \(U\) with distinct roots, the curve \(v^2=U(u)\) has genus one, and \(t-t_0=\pm\int_{u_0}^u ds/\sqrt{U(s)}\) gives the nutation locally; its inversion is elliptic. Multiple-root and degree-drop cases degenerate and require separate elementary limiting formulas.

title: Right-quantized symbol and order
notes: This lecture displays the kernel using \(\sigma(y,\xi)\), and repeats the low-frequency cutoff and \(H^{\ell+s}\to H^\ell\) convention.
statement: Right quantization is \(Au(x)=(2\pi)^{-n}\iint e^{i(x-y)\cdot\xi}\sigma(y,\xi)u(y)\,dy\,d\xi\). Smooth order-\(s\) symbols give the indicated Sobolev loss under proper-support or uniform global hypotheses.

title: Product symbol and scalar commutator order
notes: \(AB\) has symbol \(\sigma_1\sigma_2\) modulo a subordinate operator.
statement: For smooth classical operators of orders \(s_1,s_2\), the product principal symbol is \(\sigma_{s_1}(A)\sigma_{s_2}(B)\). If the leading symbols commute, in particular for scalar operators, \([A,B]\) has order at most \(s_1+s_2-1\).

statement: Both \(\varphi A\) and \(A\varphi\) have principal symbol \(\varphi\sigma_s(A)\); their difference has order at most \(s-1\).

title: Separated cutoffs eliminate the principal symbol
notes: For separated \(\varphi,\psi\), \(\varphi A\psi\) is subordinate, with a one-order Sobolev gain displayed.
statement: If \(\varphi\psi=0\), the order-\(s\) principal symbol of \(\varphi A\psi\) vanishes. If their supports are disjoint, the smooth calculus gives an infinitely smoothing operator, a stronger assertion than the recorded one-order gain.
reconstruction: Pointwise vanishing product and disjoint closed supports are distinguished; only the latter immediately gives the full off-diagonal smoothing statement.

title: Vanishing principal symbol does not annihilate every operator
notes: A smoothing order-zero operator is said to have zero symbol and therefore to vanish.
statement: An operator of order zero with improved Sobolev order has zero principal order-zero symbol. In the full calculus this means that it belongs to a lower-order class; it need not be zero. Only the restricted model with a sole exactly homogeneous symbol and no independent remainder has the asserted injectivity.
reconstruction: \ours{} A nonzero operator with a smooth compactly supported kernel is a direct counterexample to the unrestricted conclusion. The recorded proof uses a positive symbol obtained from the adjoint product and angular changes of variables; positivity after finitely many angular localizations detects a nonzero principal symbol. This justifies symbol vanishing, not the disappearance of an arbitrary lower-order remainder.
fate: The kernel of the principal-symbol map is explicitly the lower-order class in \citet{seeley1965bundles}, Theorem 7.1.
present_status: As of November 2026: established under the stated hypotheses; no unresolved problem is asserted by this occurrence.

title: Change of coordinates and cotangent transformation
notes: The symbol transforms like the highest characteristic polynomial of a differential operator.
statement: Under \(y=\kappa(x)\), the transformed principal symbol is \[\widetilde\sigma(y,\eta)=\sigma(\kappa^{-1}(y),D\kappa(\kappa^{-1}(y))^T\eta)\]. Bundle frames transform by the corresponding source and target changes of basis. Quantization corrections have order at most \(s-1\).

title: Historical attributions in the calculus

title: Double boundary cosine integral for planar area
notes: With the normals drawn at \(M,N\), \(\iint\cos\varphi_M\cos\varphi_N\,dM\,dN=2\pi S\), where \(S\) is area.

A complete independent derivation is included in the audit notes. A second independent proof uses the divergence theorem and the flux of the logarithmic potential. The circle normalization check is an independent computation, \oursComputed{}.
